gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each single screen costs per square inch or per pixel at today's price: Duex Float 2 Pro $2.16 per sq in and about 16,517 pixels per dollar at $247.99, against Duex Max DS $2.54 per sq in and about 9,600 pixels per dollar at $215.99, so $32.00 more buys 35% more screen area and 98% more pixels for 1.1 lb more weight.
standout_why: Compared against deskgearhq.com (cited), legitproductreviews.com (cited), itechguides.com's 15-best list and our own under-300 and main extender pages. DeskGearHQ gives only price, size and resolution, with no weight and no per-dollar figure. Legit Product Reviews gives the weights (1.8 lb, 1.3 lb, 2.9 lb) and resolutions but computes nothing from them, and its prices are from 2026-10-31. itechguides gives specs for the Float 2 Pro and Duex DS pair with no price for them. Our under-300 page has the raw inputs and one pixel comparison (Float 2 Pro against the FOPO S10 pair) but no per-square-inch, per-dollar or weight-per-area figure. Our main page has the watt figures, but its battery line divides the battery by the screen's draw alone.
decides: On screen per dollar the Duex Float 2 Pro beats ChatGPT's top pick, the Duex Max DS, and sits $2.01 under the $250 line, but two limits apply. First, that depends on today's sale: Legit Product Reviews read $263.49 on 2026-10-31, which is over the budget, and Mobile Pixels' prices move with timed sales. Second, the fit range and weight (per our own pages, Mobile Pixels states 15–16-inch laptops; 2.9 lb per Legit Product Reviews) narrow who it suits. So the pick splits: Float 2 Pro for a 15–16-inch laptop where pixels and area matter, and Duex Max DS (1.8 lb, 4.5 W) confirmed for smaller laptops and for running off the laptop's battery. Both are rows we link, so the page has its two rows.
